description: Module-level functions for starting the bot and reading its data files.

functions.name: run

params.name: bot
params.description: The bot class, or a factory where the language has no class objects (C++: template argument).

functions.description: Entry point and the only call in the bot's main. Creates one bot instance, speaks the protocol and returns when the game is over. Transport and log level come from command-line arguments or environment, so the same file runs locally, in a debugger and on the server (E61): --tcp [PORT] connects to 127.0.0.1 (default port 7470) instead of using stdin/stdout, --log-level LEVEL sets the start level (trace, debug, info, warn, error, off), --log-file PATH also writes the log to a file. The environment variables SBM_TRANSPORT (stdio or tcp), SBM_PORT, SBM_LOG_LEVEL and SBM_LOG_FILE do the same; arguments win. Without either the bot uses stdio and INFO. --remote URL plays against a bot on the server at URL instead (E116): with an API token of a coder from --token or, better, SBM_TOKEN, the opponent's name from --opponent, the own color from --color (white, black or random, the default) and either a discipline by name from --discipline or free times from --time SECONDS+INCREMENT (default 60+1); SBM_TRANSPORT=remote with SBM_REMOTE_URL, SBM_OPPONENT, SBM_COLOR, SBM_DISCIPLINE and SBM_TIME do the same. The SDK asks the web API for the game, joins its seat over WebSocket and then speaks the same protocol; the clock runs on the server and includes the network's delay. Other arguments are left to the bot.

functions.name: load_data

params.name: name
params.description: File name without directory, as uploaded.

functions.description: Reads a data file uploaded with the bot (E30); the only way to read files. It reads from the directory named by the environment variable SBM_DATA_DIR, which the server sets; without it from the directory data next to the bot's main file (E62). Names that are empty, contain / or \ or are equal to . or .. are invalid.
